findings.reason: declaring s14←s12, s17←s13 and s19←s12 as typed edges would let the roadmap hold the dependent sections instead of relying on a coordinator reading the prose, and it removes the same-file write collision a parallel wave would otherwise hit.
findings.text: the declared section graph carries only s15's cross-plan edge, while §14 ("dispatch this section after §12 lands", line 128), §17 ("dispatch this section after §13 lands", line 140) and §19 ("dispatch this section after §12 lands", line 148) each wait on a sibling because they write a file inside that sibling's write path (§14 writes picker/outcomes.py and §19 writes prompts.py/snapshot.py, both inside §12's reckon/crew/picker/; §17 writes reckon/ledger.py, §13's path); the wait is expressible in plan-section-depends-on or the section record's links but is left as prose, so a roadmap read shows all of s12–s19 as independently dispatchable

findings.reason: a node can close §13 on its done-when with item 4 silently skipped, and the docstring/orphan-sweep contradiction the section exists to fix stays. Item 4's gap is the sharp instance of a wider pattern: only §16 declares a red arm ("fails when a test is made to spawn codex"), so s12, s13, s14, s15, s17, s18 and s19 each need a named control before their guards can be shown to fire.
findings.text: §13's done-when opens "tests prove the first three items" while the section lists four work items, so item 4 (the crew gc --scratch docstring reconciliation, verified against routing.py:2102-2110 versus the age-keyed sweep at :1943) has no clause that fails if it is left undone

findings.reason: the section's entire evidence is the replay of that pick; without the run id the node must hunt the ledger for an under-specified event and may replay the wrong one, which is the failure of an anchor that names nothing resolvable.
findings.text: §19 is built on one specific event ("On 2026-10-08, Jev held a review dispatch with a hold probability of 0.83 ... The coordinator overrode it with --local") and its first work item is to "Replay the recorded state of that pick", but it names no run id, node or ledger row for the pick, so the node dispatched to it cannot locate the state to replay

findings.reason: the section points a node at dispatch_picker.py while the stage it wants to fix is picker/__init__.py:281 and times a different quantity; correcting the cause (the estimate_ms stage times a trivial rendered-length estimate, not the context estimate) is what lets the fix and its done-when ("a pick which ran an estimate records a non-zero estimate_ms") actually measure an estimate.
findings.text: §12 states "estimate_ms reads 0 on every pick, because the estimate runs in reckon/crew/dispatch_picker.py before pick() starts that stage's clock", but the estimate_ms stage does run and is closed by pick() itself: reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:281-283 wraps a trivial in-process computation (`token_estimate = math.ceil(len(rendered) / 4)`) in its own perf_counter, which reads as 0 ms regardless of where estimated_context_tokens runs; a node implementing item 3 against the stated cause can time the real estimate in dispatch_picker.py and still leave the estimate_ms stage measuring the len/4 quantity, so the section's stated root cause does not match the code and the fix can miss the stage it names
